---
title: "The difference between two date-times changes unit with the gap"
ref: DAT-05
categories: [Dates]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`90` seconds, then `45` seconds"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
start <- as.POSIXct("2026-10-23 10:00:00", tz = "UTC")
end_1 <- as.POSIXct("2026-10-23 10:01:30", tz = "UTC")
end_2 <- as.POSIXct("2026-10-23 10:00:45", tz = "UTC")

as.numeric(end_1 - start)
as.numeric(end_2 - start)
```
:::

## Why

Subtracting two date-times calls `difftime()` with `units = "auto"`. R then picks the most readable unit: seconds under a minute, minutes under an hour, then hours, days, weeks. The first gap is 1.5 *minutes*, the second 45 *seconds*.

The printout says so ("Time difference of 1.5 mins"), but `as.numeric()` throws the unit away and keeps only the number. On a vector, the unit depends on the smallest gap: adding or removing a row can change the unit of the whole column.

## The remedy

Choose the unit explicitly, when computing or when converting.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
as.numeric(difftime(end_1, time2 = start, units = "secs"))
as.numeric(end_2 - start, units = "secs")
```
:::
